questions.question: A developer is typing inside a function in src/cart.js in Visual Studio Code. Which three sources of context can the Copilot extension include when it builds the prompt for an inline suggestion? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: The file name and programming language
options.why: Correct. The file name and language tell the model what kind of code to write.

options.text: Related snippets from other files open in editor tabs
options.why: Correct. Open tabs are used to find related code.

options.text: Every file in every repository the developer can access
options.why: The context window is limited, so the extension selects context. It does not send every repository.

options.text: Files covered by a content exclusion
options.why: Excluded files are not used as context in supported IDEs.

options.text: Code before and after the cursor
options.why: Correct. The code on both sides of the cursor is the main context for a completion.

questions.explanation: Inline suggestions use nearby code, the file name and language, and related snippets from open tabs.

questions.question: Why does the Copilot extension rank and trim context before it sends a prompt?

options.text: Trimming removes all comments so the model only sees code.
options.why: Comments are useful context and are not removed by design.

options.text: The model can process only a limited amount of text in one request.
options.why: Correct. The context window is limited, so the most relevant context is kept.

options.text: GitHub charges per character sent in each prompt.
options.why: Copilot plans are not billed per character of context.

options.text: The proxy rejects any prompt longer than one file.
options.why: There is no one-file rule. The limit is the model's context window.

questions.explanation: Models have a limited context window, so the extension picks the most relevant context for each request.

questions.question: A developer asks Copilot Chat about a bug, and the answer ignores src/discount.js. The developer wants to confirm which files were used to produce the answer. What should the developer do?

options.text: Open the organization audit log and search for action:copilot.
options.why: The audit log records administrative events, not the context of individual answers.

options.text: Run /clear and ask the same question again.
options.why: Clearing the chat starts fresh but does not show which files were used.

options.text: Check the Copilot status bar icon.
options.why: The status icon shows Copilot's state, such as signed in or excluded, not answer references.

options.text: Expand Used n references below the answer.
options.why: Correct. The references list shows the files and snippets used as context.

questions.explanation: Used n references lists the context that went into a chat answer.

questions.question: A developer writes tests in tests/discount.test.js, but inline suggestions keep using function names from an unrelated file. Several old files are open in other tabs. What should the developer do first?

options.text: Ask an administrator to exclude the tests folder.
options.why: Excluding the folder would stop suggestions in the tests entirely.

options.text: Close unrelated tabs and open src/discount.js in a tab.
options.why: Correct. Open tabs are used as context, so relevant tabs help and unrelated ones can mislead.

options.text: Disable Copilot for JavaScript in github.copilot.enable.
options.why: That turns off suggestions instead of improving them.

options.text: Change the public code filter to Allow.
options.why: The public code filter affects matches with public code, not which local files are used as context.

questions.explanation: Inline suggestions draw on open tabs, so keeping relevant files open and closing unrelated ones improves results.

questions.question: In Copilot Chat, a developer wants Copilot to search the whole workspace for code related to a question about discount codes. Which context should the developer add to the prompt?

options.text: #selection
options.why: #selection adds only the code currently highlighted in the editor.

options.text: #terminalLastCommand
options.why: This adds the last terminal command and its output, not workspace code.

options.text: /clear
options.why: /clear starts a new conversation. It does not add context.

options.text: #codebase
options.why: Correct. #codebase searches the workspace and adds relevant code to the prompt.

questions.explanation: #codebase (or the @workspace participant) brings relevant code from across the workspace into the chat prompt.
